question.problem: Let $x=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 7 \\ -6 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ and $a=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ If $x=y+z,$ where $y\in \text{Span}{a}$ and $z⊥\text{Span}{a},$ then $z=$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14121442/assets/d887852fe51f08cb7296437e69b6a9632721cfd155558e6abf9a99b4f59f7ad6.png)

First, we find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{a}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{a}\,x & =\frac{a\cdot x}{a\cdot a}a \\  & =\frac{2\cdot 3+3\cdot 7+(-3)(-6)+1\cdot 1}{{2}^{2}+{3}^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{1}^{2}}a \\  & =\frac{6+21+18+1}{4+9+9+1}a \\  & =\frac{46}{23}a \\  & =2a \\  & =2[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 6 \\ -6 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we get the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={\text{proj}}_{a}\,x=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 6 \\ -6 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ z & =x-{\text{proj}}_{a}\,x=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 7 \\ -6 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 6 \\ -6 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $y\in \text{Span}{a}$ and $z⊥\text{Span}{a},$ as shown in the picture above.

In conclusion, $z=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$
